1.explanation: The file packages/react/src/components/DataTable/TableHeader.js is directly responsible for rendering the TableHeader component, and its code contains the bug: the ...rest props are conditionally applied to <th> or <button> depending on sortability, but in the sortable case they are incorrectly applied to the button, not the th element. This prevents external props (like id or ARIA attributes) from being set on the correct DOM node for accessibility purposes. No other files are relevant for the root cause or the fix, though related tests might need updating after the fix.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario concerns the TableHeader component, where the ...rest props (intended to allow user-defined properties such as id and ARIA attributes for accessibility) are incorrectly spread onto the inner <button> element when the column is sortable, rather than onto the outer <th> element as should be the case. For non-sortable columns, ...rest is correctly spread onto <th>. This results in user props like id being applied to the wrong element for sortable headers, causing accessibility issues (such as violation of the WCAG H43 requirement that table header cells have correct id attributes). The screenshot highlights the locations in the source code where ...rest is handled for both cases and questions if it should be on <th> instead of <button>.

2.bug_scenario: The bug scenario is a prop forwarding issue in the TableHeader component of the carbon-components-react package. When TableHeader is used for sortable columns, the ...rest props (including critical accessibility props like id) are incorrectly placed on the inner button element, rather than on the <th> itself. This results in missing ids on sortable header cells, violating accessibility requirements (WCAG H43), while non-sortable header cells receive these props correctly.
